partial_progress.details: Phase Mission restricted this dispatch to Phase 1 only (5-phase plan). Phase 1 completed and committed; phases 2-5 remain for subsequent dispatches.

artifacts.summary: Phase 1 completion handoff: shared link resolver added to lib/sapience-api-lib.sh with unit coverage; next dispatch starts Phase 2.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added sapience_project_link_read and sapience_project_link_cid to agent-system/extensions/sapience/scripts/lib/sapience-api-lib.sh: a single-location .sapience/project.json resolver, taking an already-resolved toplevel, validating exactly the three string keys project/name/repo field-for-field against repo_link.py's parse_link, with no copy of the nine-copy worktree-resolution lockstep block. Added accept/reject unit cases 13-17 to test-sapience-capture.sh (43 passed, 0 failed); test-sapience-publish.sh and test-sapience-vault-read.sh still pass; grep confirms 0 copies of the lockstep block added.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience-api-lib.sh test resolution under CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE
sapience_notes.value: common_test_resolve_subject (which honors CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE) must be used to resolve a sapience-api-lib.sh test subject, never a hand-rolled deploy-then-source if/elif like test-sapience-publish.sh's own API_LIB block uses -- that hand-rolled form ignores CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE entirely. Confirmed live: with the sapience extension's deployed .claude/ tree stale relative to the source store, the hand-rolled form silently sourced the OLD deployed lib (missing newly-added functions) even with CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store set, producing rc=127 'command not found' for every new function call until switched to common_test_resolve_subject.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience-project-bind.sh write_link_file three-key validation
sapience_notes.value: repo_link.py's parse_link requires an object with EXACTLY three string keys (project/name/repo); a 'token/key/secret/password-shaped extra key' refusal is satisfied structurally by the exact-key-count check alone -- any object carrying a fourth key of any shape already fails validation, so no separate key-name-pattern check is needed to cover that case.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience worktree-checkout-resolution lockstep count
sapience_notes.value: Confirmed live via grep -rc 'BEGIN sapience-worktree-checkout-resolution' across agent-system/extensions/sapience/scripts/: exactly 9 production/verification scripts each carry one copy (sapience-vault-read.sh, sapience-remember.sh, verify-sapience-mcp.sh, sapience-publish.sh, verify-sapience-context-scoping.sh, sapience-tag-pending.sh, sapience-retrieve.sh, sapience-project-bind.sh, test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh), matching the plan's re-derived Scope Hypothesis rather than the stale 'five copies' figure in an earlier research report.
